text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has asked the House of Representatives to approve the borrowing of up to $300 million from abroad, needed to cover the shortfall on the current account from 1996.
- Angry investors sue Paneuropean for 250,000 pounds ($495,000) in an on-going dispute regarding Paneuropean warrants that expired last June but failed to be converted into partly-paid shares.
- The finance minister is paving the way for drastic changes to the income tax law to give the Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) a boost.
Other Greek Cypriot newspapers were not published on Wednesday due to the Greek National Day holiday on Tuesday, March 25.
